subject: Renewal consumption pulse + proposed stair-step uplift
content:
From: Janie Cole <janie@averysys.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Hsu <thsu@averysys.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal prep: usage spike context and ask for a recommendation

Karthik / Redwood team,

As we head into our renewal, we wanted a quick read on two things before we lock terms: 1) the recent token spike in March (see attached CSV) — was that an anomaly or a sustained shift, and 2) options for smoothing pricing if we move to a stepped commit across the next 12 months.

We saw a ~38% MoM increase in prompt tokens in March that pushed us over our current monthly buffer. We're interested in a proposal that buys predictability but still gives us headroom for a product launch scheduled in Q3.

Can you send a short recommendation and an economics outline (pricing + credits/burst mechanics) we can show to procurement? Appreciate a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Janie
Janie Cole
Head of AI Products | Avery Systems
[attachment: avery_usage_q1_2028.csv (csv)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Janie Cole <janie@averysys.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep: usage spike context and ask for a recommendation

Thanks Janie — quick first-pass summary below; attaching a one-pager with a suggested stair-step.

Short summary:
- March spike: mixed drivers. ~60% of the extra tokens were long-form generation for your new onboarding flow (warm-up campaigns); ~25% were search/rerank sampling for internal experiments; ~15% were anomalous test jobs from a mis-configured batch job. We validated the latter and blocked it on Apr 2.
- Performance: median (p50) generation latency for the quarter is 180ms, p95 is 840ms (model: rdx-6b-q4f16). No regressions tied to the spike. See rls_q1_performance.pdf for the per-route breakdown.
- Economics: if you keep a pure month-to-month posture you will incur overage volatility. A 12-month stair-step commit can reduce effective unit cost by ~9-14% depending on the initial commit band.

Proposal (high level):
- Commit ladder: start at 120M tokens/month (baseline current run-rate ~100M), +20% at month 5, +15% at month 9. Total 12-month commit ~1.5B tokens.
- Burst credits: 200M burst pool for unexpected launches (applies at enterprise tier only).
- Optimization: we recommend enabling prefix cache for onboarding flows and adopting 4-bit quantized model variants for non-critical endpoints — expected token-cost reduction ~6-8%.

Next steps: schedule a 30-min alignment demo + MAP (mutual action plan) for procurement. I can put together the clean addendum and pricing grid for review.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_stairstep_addendum_v2.pdf (pdf), rls_q1_performance.pdf (pdf)]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Janie Cole <janie@averysys.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep: usage spike context and ask for a recommendation

Janie — quick technical notes to supplement Karthik's econ summary: feel free to forward to your infra folks.

- Root cause analysis: the mis-configured batch job was hitting a non-throttled /generate endpoint with long prompt templates. We implemented a server-side guard on Apr 2 that rejects >16k token batch prompts for non-admin clients.
- Caching opportunity: onboarding flow looks like 45% prefix-reuse. Enabling KV prefix caching on those routes will cut token count on average by ~28% for those calls. We'll produce a small config change and monitor for 2 weeks in staging.
- Model variants: moving the low-sensitivity routes to our rdx-6b-q4.0 path reduces compute latency slightly and is fully compatible with your output fidelity needs (we A/B'd on a random sample).

I'll schedule a technical sync with your engineer (Tom) to run the config change and snapshot metrics.

-sean
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep: usage spike context and ask for a recommendation

Janie — pulling in pricing/finance context for procurement. Two clarifications re: the addendum Karthik shared:

1) Effective unit pricing: presented as $28/1M tokens in month 1 band (120M committed), sliding to $24/1M at the month-9 uplift (aggregate weighted price ~ $25.7/1M). We can show a compare-to-overage scenario in the MAP.
2) Credits & terms: burst credits are reconciled monthly; unused burst credits do not roll beyond the 12-month term. Standard invoice cadence is monthly with net-30. If procurement needs an alternate cadence (quarterly in arrears) we can explore a minor uplift to the rate.

Attached is the proposed addendum v2 that contains the price table and the MAP draft. I'll update it after the technical sync.

-Naomi
